title: KV cache priming compatibility matrix and preflight harness
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Objective: build a preflight validation harness that verifies KV cache priming and compatibility across runtime versions and model kernel variants. Motivation: recent upgrades to kernel selection and cache layout have changed key eviction ordering and memory layout, causing cold-start latency regressions in a subset of models. This ticket establishes an automated suite that runs smoke checks, perf regression gates, and deterministic evals against a compatibility matrix (version x model-family x hardware-profile) before rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- A compatibility matrix generator that enumerates supported runtime versions, model families (causal, chat, encoder-only), quantization formats, and representative hardware profiles (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, T4) as CSV artifact.
- A KV priming harness that can: (1) replay synthesized prefix workloads to establish expected KV shapes; (2) validate that primed cache produces identical generation latencies and token deltas within SLOs; (3) detect silent key-shifts (hash/mapping changes) that would invalidate prefix cache hits.
- Smoke checks for each matrix cell that assert critical path latencies (p50/p95) and token-throughput are within baseline + permitted delta.
- Perf regression gate that compares current candidate build against baseline build with configurable thresholds and automatic block/rollout signal if exceeded.
- Eval suite of curated prompts that measure output quality drift for primed vs cold runs (BLEU/ROUGE proxies + model-specific heuristics).
- Integration with rollout orchestration: results surface as pass/fail to canary gating API with links to generated artifacts and dashboards.

Plan:
1) Implement matrix generator (ENG-31207 is a dependency for canonical hardware profiles).
2) Prototype KV priming harness as lightweight runner (Python + Rust bridge) and iterate on performance instrumentation.
3) Wire smoke checks and perf regression comparator using CI infra (GitHub Actions -> internal test runner).
4) Add automated publishing of CSV matrix, per-cell artifacts (logs, flamegraphs), and a dashboard tile.
5) Add canary gate hook to rollout API to block canaries when perf or quality regressions are detected.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Priming long prefixes reduces cold-start pain but increases memory pressure; we will tune priming window and track eviction metrics.
- Strict perf thresholds can increase false positives during noisy infra; we will implement rolling baselines and require persistent regression across 3 runs for gating.
- Full coverage of all model/kernel/hw combinations is expensive; initial rollout will focus on high-traffic model families and critical hardware profiles.
